intro: Compress PDF makes a document lighter so you can email it, upload it to a portal with a size limit or simply store it using less space. Most of the weight of a PDF usually comes from photos and scans, so the tool saves those images again at the resolution and quality you pick while leaving the text untouched: it stays selectable and searchable.

The balanced level brings images down to 144 dpi at 75% quality, which is plenty for reading on screen and printing at home. The strong level goes to 96 dpi and 60%, meant for very large attachments. Lossless leaves images alone and removes duplicated objects, thumbnails and unused resources. Custom lets you set the maximum resolution and JPEG quality yourself.

Under more options you can strip metadata, attachments, annotations, bookmarks or the accessibility structure, turn images grey or flatten forms. Some of those boxes have side effects: removing tags breaks accessibility and removing output intents means the file is no longer PDF/A, and the result tells you when that happens.
If the file was already optimised and the compressed copy would be the same size or larger, you get the original back with a note. That way you never download a PDF bigger than the one you uploaded.

faq.a: Only in images, and only as much as you choose. Text and vector graphics are kept as they are. For maximum fidelity, use the lossless level.

faq.q: Can I compress several PDFs at once?
faq.a: Yes. You get each compressed file separately plus a ZIP with all of them.

faq.q: What if the PDF has a password?
faq.a: Type it under more options. It is only used to open the file during the task and is never stored.
On our server in the European Union. The file travels encrypted and is deleted automatically after one hour without an account, or after 24 hours with one.
